# ImmersivePoints

> A free web viewer that shows 3D point clouds on desktop and in VR headsets (Quest, PC VR, any WebXR browser). It is driven entirely by its URL: an agent can turn a numpy array into one shareable link, with no upload, account or server.

Full guide for agents: https://immersivepoints.meertens.dev/for-ai-agents.html

## Quick recipe (Python, needs only numpy)

    curl -O https://immersivepoints.meertens.dev/examples/viewer_link.py

    import numpy as np
    from viewer_link import fit_to_view, hue_from_values, viewer_link
    xyz = fit_to_view(my_xyz)          # (N, 3): centered, about 8 units across, Y up
    hue = hue_from_values(my_values)   # (N,): hue 0 (red) to 0.55 (cyan)
    print(viewer_link(np.column_stack([xyz, hue])))

## Link format

1. Rows of float32 per point: x, y, z, hue (type XYZI) or x, y, z, r, g, b (type XYZRGB). Hue and RGB are 0 to 1.
2. Encode the rows as BIG-ENDIAN float32 (numpy astype(">f4")), then base64.
3. Config JSON: {"points": [{"source": "base64", "base64": "<data>", "type": "XYZI", "pointSize": 0.04}]}
   For a hosted file: {"points": [{"source": "url", "url": "https://.../scan.xyzrgb", "type": "XYZRGB"}]}
   The host must send CORS headers (raw.githubusercontent.com, GitHub Pages, S3 or GCS with CORS). Cloudini .cldn files use "type": "CLOUDINI".
4. Link: https://immersivepoints.meertens.dev/oculus.html#jsonb64=<URL-encoded base64 of the config JSON>
   Use "#" so the data never reaches a server (no server URL length limit). "?jsonb64=" also works for short links.

Single hosted file shortcut: https://immersivepoints.meertens.dev/oculus.html?url=<file URL>&mode=xyzi|xyzrgb|cloudini (mode only if the extension does not say).
Extra URL parameters: autoRotate=true (desktop rotation), showAxes=true (X red, Y green, Z blue). Leave them out to turn them off.
Optional config keys: "bboxes" and "lines" (first entry, url source only), "objects" (glTF/GLB with position, rotation, scale).
Box files: 13 big-endian float32 per box (center xyz, size xyz, rotation xyz in radians, r, g, b, opacity). Line files: 6 per segment (start xyz, end xyz).

## Making it look good

- Y is up. Rotate Z-up data (LiDAR, ROS, GIS, CAD) with (x, y, z) -> (x, z, -y).
- Desktop camera is 20 units from the origin and sees about 9.5 units vertically: center the data and scale its largest side to about 8 (use 1st-99th percentiles, not min/max).
- In VR the person starts at the origin on the floor y = 0, looking toward -Z. For walk-through scenes keep metres and put the ground at y = 0.
- Point size (pointSize, default 0.04): 0.06-0.1 for under 20k points, 0.04 for 20k-300k, 0.02-0.03 for dense scans.
- Background is blue (#2d4aa8): avoid hues 0.58-0.78. Continuous values: hue 0 to 0.55. Categories: distinct hues that skip blue.
- XYZRGB colors are 0-1 floats; lift very dark colors (0.15 + 0.85 * rgb).
- Keep under about 500k points for standalone headsets; subsample or host a Cloudini file for more.
- Inline data costs about 28 link characters per XYZI point and 43 per XYZRGB point: inline up to about 30k points, host a file beyond that.

## Checking a link

The browser console prints "Loaded num points N" on success. Errors appear as a red panel (for example "Data Parsing Error", "File Not Found", "Network Error") with details.
